title: What looping a released model adds, by who measured it
takeaway: Searched cells gained up to 2.6 points. A label-free check found 0.6 to 2, not significant; a 14B gained 0.8 to 4.2.

rows.label: Qwen3-4B, MMLU-Pro, best of a search
Qwen3-14B, GSM8K
rows.note: 90.2% against the unlooped 8B's 89.4%

rows.label: Qwen3-14B, MATH-500
rows.note: 80.2% against 76.0%, at about 1.3x the looped 8B's time

caption: Accuracy gained over the same model without the loop, in points. The authors' cells come from a per-cell search over about 720 settings, except the 30B rows, which were fixed in advance; one 30B cell, GPQA-Diamond, lost 1.5 points. The check placed its loop without benchmark answers. The 14B rows show a bigger model instead, at about 1.3 times the looped 8B's time.

title: What a translated cache costs in accuracy
takeaway: Moving a cache between models loses 2 to 3% on short contexts, 8% at 32,000 tokens and 17% at 128,000.

caption: Share of the receiving model's accuracy lost against re-reading the text, each on its own models and tasks. What it buys: the first token 2.5 to 7.5x sooner at long contexts, 30 to 98% lower first-token time under load, and a mapping 2.7 to 25x faster than a re-read. All three are the authors' own numbers on models of 8 to 32 billion parameters.
